title: ARP packet (RFC 826)
summary: An ARP (Address Resolution Protocol) packet resolves an IPv4 address to a MAC address (and reverse). Layout: hardware type (2), protocol type (2), hardware address length (1), protocol address length (1), operation (2: 1 request, 2 reply), sender hardware address (6), sender protocol address (4), target hardware address (6), target protocol address (4). Total 28 bytes for Ethernet/IPv4.

ext.summary: An ARP (Address Resolution Protocol) packet resolves an IPv4 address to a MAC address (and reverse). Layout: hardware type (2), protocol type (2), hardware address length (1), protocol address length (1), operation (2: 1 request, 2 reply), sender hardware address (6), sender protocol address (4), target hardware address (6), target protocol address (4). Total 28 bytes for Ethernet/IPv4.

structure.meaning: 1 = request, 2 = reply, 3 = RARP request, 4 = RARP reply.

notes: ARP request is broadcast (dst MAC FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF); reply is unicast.
Gratuitous ARP: sender and target IP are the same, used for IP conflict detection and cache updates.
ARP cache entries expire (typically 1-20 minutes); stale entries cause brief packet loss.
RARP (operation 3/4) is obsolete; DHCP replaced it.
Proxy ARP: a router answers ARP on behalf of another host.
